explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM-as-judge (DeepSeek-v3) against human evaluation for free-form justification questions using three complementary matching methods, with quantitative comparison of performance across evaluation formats

prompts.notes: LLM-as-judge was used only for free-form response evaluation (matching responses to closest option), but specific judging prompts are not provided

per_criterion.notes: 7/100 received individual flags but none reached majority disapproval

guidelines.notes: Guidelines included coherence, safety, and white lie authenticity assessment using binary assessment with written explanations; qualification tests used to filter annotators

sample_size.notes: Validation focuses specifically on justification questions comparing MCQ format versus free-form responses evaluated by three methods including LLM-as-judge

quantitative_scores.notes: Performance drops significantly in free-form responses
One of three matching methods used

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-as-judge shows substantial performance gap compared to human evaluation on justification tasks, with models struggling to independently infer prosocial intentions behind white lies without MCQ guidance

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM-as-judge was used specifically for evaluating free-form responses against human-validated ground truth, while humans handled broader quality assessment
